sources.name: OSGB36 / British National Grid — EPSG:27700
verified_facts: EPSG:27700 is the valid projected CRS OSGB36 / British National Grid.
Its coordinate system is Cartesian 2D with easting and northing axes measured in metres.
Its stated scope includes engineering survey and topographic mapping.
semantic_limits: EPSG:27700 defines horizontal positioning and does not by itself specify an ODN vertical height datum.
A correct CRS identifier does not prove that a parcel polygon or elevation sample is correct.

sources.name: OSGB36 / British National Grid + ODN height — EPSG:7405
verified_facts: EPSG:7405 is the compound CRS OSGB36 / British National Grid + ODN height.
The vertical component is ODN height EPSG:5701 with a gravity-related height axis in metres.
semantic_limits: Compound CRS identification prevents horizontal and vertical reference conflation but does not alter raster values.
The parcel result still requires exact polygon binding, source-byte hashing and valid-pixel sampling.

sources.name: ETRS89 to OSGB36 / British National Grid (3) — EPSG:7953
verified_facts: EPSG:7953 is the OSTN15-based ETRS89-to-OSGB36 British National Grid transformation.
It is identified as the official definition of OSGB36 from August 2016.
The registry distinguishes exactness by definition from comparison accuracy against archived triangulation coordinates.
semantic_limits: Exactness by definition is a reference-frame statement and is not parcel-elevation measurement accuracy.
Transformation accuracy must remain separate from LiDAR vertical RMSE and polygon uncertainty.

sources.name: Converting grid eastings/northings and ellipsoidal latitude/longitude
verified_facts: Conversion between latitude/longitude and eastings/northings on the same datum is a map projection operation.
That operation is not a datum transformation.
GNSS/ETRS89 to OSGB36 National Grid conversion requires OSTN15 or an explicitly lower-accuracy approximation.
semantic_limits: A projection formula must not be substituted for a datum transformation.
WGS84 display coordinates remain unsuitable for exact parcel containment when native British National Grid geometry is available.
